> **Before you read (corrected 2026-09)**: these are course notes from the webpack 4 → 5 era; the frame of reference stops around 2021.
> Back then webpack was the default and the argument was "4 or 5".
> In 2026 webpack is still maintained (5.110.3, released 2026-09-01) but it is no longer the default — the Rust toolchain took that: Rspack 2.2.2, Vite 8.2.2.
> The internals here (IIFE bundles, `__webpack_require__`, the tapable lifecycle, the cost of passing strings between loaders) have not aged and are still worth knowing.
> For specific plugin advice and version facts, trust the **Correction** blocks below — several claims in the original are simply wrong.

[https://ke.qq.com/webcourse/1647350/103691469#taid=12145403010556662&vid=387702293148710449](https://ke.qq.com/webcourse/1647350/103691469#taid=12145403010556662&vid=387702293148710449)

Video playback engines are all WebAssembly now.

Webpack's weak spot is JavaScript. JavaScript runs in a JIT, and it needs an engine to run at all.

That is the environment Webpack lives in, and its speed is capped by the JS engine.

Badly written JavaScript makes Webpack slow. But however much you optimise, you have already handed the work to a black box.

**OSS** — cloud object storage.

**Jump box (bastion host)** — sits between the internal network and the outside, controlling how external users or admins reach the inside. Its main job is to harden the internal network. It also works as a central node for managing and monitoring internal servers and devices.

# Optimising Webpack 4

## I/O

### Upgrade Webpack itself

Webpack is slow mostly because I/O is slow.

Webpack does a lot of I/O — constant input and output.

Frequent I/O is what makes it slow, so keep the entry small and stop the I/O growing.

(This matters for the dev server's HMR, for persistent caching, and for the packing entry that reads a pile of files out of a directory.)

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1683950102061-2873ced5-4e73-4f32-834b-a2e0edd895b6.png" width="470.4" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="u70de9e1f" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

There are only two reasons for a blank page: **the JavaScript threw, or the request never came back.** If the request never came back you get a spinner.

`eval` emits code fast but runs slowly in the browser.

What `eval` gives you: 1. dynamic execution; 2. its own scope — each module goes into an `eval` function, so modules stay isolated from one another.

What it costs: a string has to be turned into code before it runs, which is slow, and it is not safe.

Webpack's dev-mode bundle uses `eval` to speed up bundling and execution and to cut both code size and transfer time.

### Many entries? Build across machines. scripty

+ **Cluster builds**

Set up passwordless SSH between your machine and three machines in the office. When the app is ready to build, send commands to all three, let them build in turn, and `scp` the results back. One machine's workload is now spread across four.

> **Dated**: the idea (spread the build out) is sound, but hand-rolled `scp` clusters are gone. Today's equivalent is remote caching plus task orchestration in CI — Turborepo/Nx remote cache, Bazel, or a GitHub Actions matrix with a shared cache. The goal shifted from "spread the compute" to "never recompute what was already computed".

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1683914069486-7484e841-b437-45f3-8583-e1d83f7f2531.png" width="500" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="u31ccd0e0" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

### Tree shaking

You have to set `optimization.usedExports` before unused code is actually removed from the output.

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1684227100768-050f9dee-5217-4cac-bc75-86d056ce1c53.png" width="500" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="u0b5034fe" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

### prepack-webpack-plugin

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1684226502119-13e93d0e-fed6-4ae7-a464-5421e11a7e1c.png" width="450" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="u4c564373" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

~~**Webpack 5 absorbed Prepack — a static JavaScript evaluator. Pure functions get evaluated away at build time.**~~

> **Correction**: webpack never absorbed Prepack. Prepack was a separate Facebook project; its last npm release was **0.2.54 on 2018-10-08** and it has been dead since, as has prepack-webpack-plugin.
> webpack 5 does do compile-time constant folding and inner-graph analysis, but that is its own implementation and has nothing to do with Prepack.
> **Do not mention Prepack in an interview** — it dates the notes.

### Why do production builds take so long?

**Production code takes longer to run and is more complex, and minification costs time.**

**For production, combine a hosted SDK with a production build to get the final result.** (So do not assume that a performance problem in development means one in production.)

### Too much currying leaks memory — currying is closures underneath.

## Caching

**Caching trades space for time, and it does waste space. These days the cache sits in memory.**

### cache-loader

**It caches everything. Anything that has not changed is not recompiled, which shortens babel-loader's work too.**

**Turning it on in Webpack 4 makes an immediate difference. Webpack 5 has it built in.**

### hard-source-webpack-plugin

**Caches the whole project** — loaders, plugins, compilation. It gets faster the more you use it, and it is said to beat cache-loader. It no longer works on Webpack 5.

> **Correction**: saying cache-loader was "merged into webpack 5" is imprecise. What actually happened is that webpack 5's built-in `cache.type = 'filesystem'` **replaced its use case**; cache-loader itself was never merged in and has been frozen at 4.1.0 since 2019-07-18.

~~Webpack's ecosystem beats Vite's. It absorbs other tools' features.~~

> **Correction**: true in 2021, inverted by 2026. Vue, Nuxt, SvelteKit and Astro all default to Vite, and Vite 8 swapped its bundler for Rolldown (written in Rust); on the React side Next.js ships Turbopack.
> webpack's position today is "the stable choice for existing projects", not "the one absorbing everyone else's features".

## Mechanics

### Multithreading: terser-webpack-plugin (minification can go parallel)

Be careful with threads in JavaScript — turning them on can make the build *slower*.

JS threads are expensive, and switching between them costs a lot.

**happypack** — the Webpack 4 plugin for parallel builds.

**Webpack 5 replaced it with thread-loader.**

+ **The compile pipeline, in miniature**

```javascript
function compile(sourceCode) {
  const tokens = tokenize(sourceCode);
  const ast = parse(tokens);
  const optimizedAst = optimize(ast);
  const targetCode = generate(optimizedAst);
  return targetCode;
}
```

### Getting out of JavaScript entirely: esbuild-loader, swc-loader

**Stop running the compilation through the JIT and do it in a lower-level language.** Babel is written in JavaScript, so it has to go through the JIT and is necessarily slow. Go and Rust are far faster.

**esbuild is written in Go and has its own tree shaking.**

> **Correction**: the original claimed a conflict with "webpack 5's Prepack" — the premise is false, webpack has no Prepack.
> The real trade-off: esbuild-loader only transpiles and minifies, it does **not** type-check (you still need `tsc`), and its tree-shaking semantics do not exactly match webpack's own `usedExports` analysis — whichever runs later in the chain wins.
> Current state: esbuild-loader 4.5.0 (2026-06-15) and swc-loader 0.2.7 (2026-01-14) are both actively maintained, so this recommendation itself still holds.

**swc is written in Rust and replaces Babel. With it, you get roughly the same speed as babel-loader with hard-source-webpack-plugin enabled.**

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1683964256100-c92e127f-6c5c-4b3a-9539-def711463686.png" width="300" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="ua4c34f18" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">swc-loader in place of Babel.

# Optimising Webpack 5

### ~~Webpack 5 builds in parallel out of the box. Set `parallel: true`. The threading is built on the Worker Pool API.~~

> **Correction**: webpack does **not** build in parallel out of the box, and still does not as of 5.110.3.
> `parallel: true` is an option on **terser-webpack-plugin**. It only affects **minification**, not compilation, and it is on by default (concurrency = CPU count − 1).
> Parallelism during compilation still means thread-loader (below).

### thread-loader

(**Even though Webpack 5 has parallel builds built in, thread-loader is still worth using.** It moves expensive tasks onto worker threads — **not** web workers — for parallel processing, which speeds the build up further. It can compile and bundle JavaScript, CSS, Less, Sass and more across several worker threads.)

**thread-loader uses child processes — not threads, and not web workers.**

> **Correction**: verified by unpacking `thread-loader@4.0.4` — `dist/WorkerPool.js` calls `child_process.spawn(process.execPath, ...)`, so it spawns **separate Node processes**.
> "Worker threads" and "Worker Pool API" are both wrong here; it has nothing to do with `worker_threads`. The "thread" in the name is historical.
> Follow the consequence through: processes can only exchange strings, so the serialisation cost is real — on small projects thread-loader makes builds *slower*.

### Persistent caching and incremental builds — why HMR is fast in dev

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1684225979489-2e54a0b3-fde0-4b2c-83f2-593a10abf612.png" width="500" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="MVcqi" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

**`cache.type = filesystem`** — persistent cache

> **Correction**: ~~`cache.provided = true`~~ **is not a real option.**
> How to check: webpack's own `schemas/WebpackOptions.json` lists 20 fields under `FileCacheOptions` (`type`, `cacheDirectory`, `buildDependencies`, `maxAge`, `compression`, `store`, `version`, …) — no `provided`.
> Incremental builds need no extra switch: `cache.type = 'filesystem'` is already incremental, and a second build reads straight from disk. What you *should* set is `cache.buildDependencies.config = [__filename]`, so the cache invalidates when the webpack config changes.

**Webpack 5's output can still contain plenty of ES6 — `let`, `const`, and so on. Babel only handles your project's code, not Webpack's own runtime.**

### ~~Prepack~~ (section void)

> **Correction**: see above — Prepack stopped being maintained in 2018 and webpack 5 never integrated it, so "tree-shake first, then let Prepack simplify the rest" describes a pipeline that does not exist.
> The modern equivalent of this step is constant folding and dead-code elimination inside **terser / swc minify / esbuild minify**.

### Static assets

**All the loaders you needed for CSS and images are gone; you just declare the file as an asset.** **If you use Less or Sass you still need loaders.**

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1683964121528-78476e13-fbf4-460d-936f-3db3894427bc.png" width="355" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="R9Ats" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

**Fonts, images, SVG — all of it handled by `type: 'asset'`.**

**`cache.type` takes two values:**

**`memory` for an in-memory cache, `filesystem` for a persistent one.**

# How Webpack works inside

## Implementing CommonJS

**A Webpack 4 bundle is an IIFE closure that implements CommonJS: every module goes into one object under a key, and you pull out whichever you need.**

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1683965678139-802e8c49-ade2-4ea9-a1e0-f07578956d02.png" width="500" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="u2e35cfc6" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1683965746352-957bb563-2ce8-46f3-826b-5856a52c92ae.png" width="500" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="u69d01748" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

`eval` is fast in development, but development performance numbers differ from a production build. Do not build your production code with your development setup — you will hit strange problems. All the dev environment has to prove is that the feature works.

**Read up on source maps, and on why `eval` is fast in development.**

Read up on the trade-offs between ESM and CommonJS.

In the finished bundle, `__webpack_require__` loads each module by `moduleId`.

## Parcel

+ Why Parcel is fast: one AST, and every loader runs against it end to end.

It converts every file into a single AST, merges all the loaders internally into one, and has them all operate on that same AST. That removes the string I/O between loaders and the repeated work.

<img src="https://cdn.nlark.com/yuque/0/2023/png/25593546/1684231135840-62365111-5b1e-439e-95e1-b2c26b59f79b.png" width="500" title="" crop="0,0,1,1" id="ube5254d0" class="ne-image" style="font-size: 22px">

+ Where Parcel fits
